events.title: Fruitvale Día de los Muertos Festival (31st annual)
events.why: The Bay Area's largest Día de los Muertos street festival, with dozens of altars, Aztec dancers, live music and great street food.

events.title: La Peña Día de Muertos Celebración: Ceremony, Ofrenda and Son Jarocho
events.venue: La Peña Cultural Center, 3105 Shattuck Ave
events.why: An intimate evening ceremony with live son jarocho music and a community ofrenda, a calmer alternative to the big street festivals.

events.title: Micailhuitl Día de Muertos Festival (22nd annual)
events.why: A big, free, all-day Día de Muertos celebration with community altars, ceremonies, crafts and food in a historic park setting kids can roam.

events.title: 45th Annual Día de los Muertos Procession in the Mission
events.why: A once-a-year candlelit walking procession through the Mission with painted faces, drums and giant puppets that older kids find memorable.

events.title: Festival of Altars (Día de los Muertos)
events.why: Dozens of large community altars built during the day, then a candlelit ceremony at 5pm and performances at 8pm; pairs with the procession nearby.

events.title: Union Square Ice Rink opening night
events.why: Opening night features on-ice performances and the first 100 guests at the 5:30pm and 7pm sessions skate free.

events.title: Downtown First Thursdays block party with Big Freedia
events.why: A free all-ages street party with DJs, food trucks and a Big Freedia set from 8 to 9pm; lively and loud, best for the older kids.

events.title: Luminous Ties public unveiling and artist celebration
events.venue: City Hall King Plaza, 250 Hamilton Ave
events.why: A ten-minute drive from Menlo Park to meet artist Kiana Honarmand and try a new interactive bench sculpture that lights up when people sit on opposite sides.

events.title: Glowfari opening night at Oakland Zoo
events.why: Seventh year of the lantern festival with hundreds of all-new animal lanterns themed around California forests, the Bay and the Everglades.

events.title: ZooLights opening night at San Francisco Zoo
events.why: The first night of the zoo's million-light walk-through, with 14 themed zones including an illuminated dinosaur exhibit.

events.title: Zoppé Italian Family Circus opening night
events.venue: Circus tent, Redwood City Public Library lot, 1044 Middlefield Rd
events.why: An old-world one-ring circus under a small big top where every seat is within 20 feet of the horses, dogs and acrobats; runs through Nov 29.

events.title: Cosmic Camp-In: Our Solar System (overnight at Chabot)
events.why: An overnight for families with hands-on science and live telescope astronomy, well suited to the 9 to 14 range.

events.title: Día de los Muertos and Diwali Festival at Crissy Field Center
events.venue: Crissy Field Center, 603 Mason St, Presidio
events.why: A free Presidio celebration combining both holidays with crafts, dance, storytelling and a fire ceremony, with the beach right outside.

events.title: Fall Train Show at the South Bay Historical Railroad Society
events.venue: Santa Clara Caltrain Station, 1005 Railroad Ave
events.why: Two running model railroads, a 1912 Pullman car, a tower for spotting real trains and live bluegrass; kids under 18 get in free.

events.title: Friends of the Los Altos Library used book sale
events.venue: New Los Altos Community Center, 97 Hillview Ave
events.why: More than 40,000 used books, puzzles and movies with a kids' play area and a $5 bag sale on Sunday, close to home.

events.title: How to Train Your Dragon: The Musical JR. (Children's Musical Theater San Jose)
events.why: A Bay Area premiere of the DreamWorks story staged by a young cast, running Nov 4 through 8 with multiple weekend showtimes.

events.title: Palo Alto Museum: First Look at Two Inaugural Exhibits (Palo Alto Stories)
events.why: A free weekend preview of the new museum's first exhibits on Juana Briones and local history, with historian talks, hands-on activities and an AI docent kids can quiz.

events.title: San Francisco Coffee Festival
events.why: Mostly for the adults: unlimited tastings from dozens of Bay Area roasters with live music, Saturday and Sunday.

events.title: San Francisco Fall Cider Fest (21+ adults only)
events.why: Adults-only (21+): unlimited tastings of about 30 craft ciders in an outdoor food-truck park, a good parents' afternoon out.

events.title: San José Roots Cultural Fest and Historic Home Tours
events.venue: San Pedro Square Market, 87 N San Pedro St
events.why: History San José opens the Peralta Adobe and Fallon House for free tours alongside Spanish and Mexican era hands-on activities and performances.

events.title: Sea Glass and Ocean Art Festival
events.why: Sixty sea glass and ocean artists in a historic building with ocean views, an easy pairing with a beach afternoon over the hill.

events.title: USA Taiwan Global Expo (Discover Taiwan)
events.venue: San Mateo County Event Center, 1346 Saratoga Dr
events.why: A cheap two-day showcase of Taiwanese street food, products and culture twenty minutes from Menlo Park.

events.title: Blankets and Blockbusters: Toy Story 5 outdoor screening
events.why: A Sunday afternoon outdoor movie on the Thrive City plaza, bring blankets.

events.title: Helicopter Adventure at Hiller Aviation Museum
events.why: A one-off helicopter-themed program at the Peninsula's aviation museum, fifteen minutes up the 101.

events.title: Muchos Art + Comic Expo (50+ artists)
events.venue: La Peña Cultural Center, 3105 Shattuck Ave
events.why: A free all-ages indie comics and zine fair with Pentel-sponsored drawing workshops, ideal for a comics-loving kid.

events.title: Redwood City Día de los Muertos Festival
events.why: Casa Círculo Cultural's free festival drew 9,000 people last year with altars, folklórico, a car display and food, ten minutes from Menlo Park.

events.title: San Francisco Diwali Festival at Yerba Buena Gardens
events.why: A free outdoor Diwali celebration with dance performances, music and food in a central downtown park.

events.title: Palo Alto Veterans Day Recognition Event
events.why: A short, free civic ceremony next door in Palo Alto, a low-key way for kids to mark Veterans Day.

events.title: Petaluma Veterans Day Parade and Huey helicopter flyover
events.why: A small-town parade with a Vietnam-era Huey landing and aircraft flyovers, the largest Veterans Day parade north of the Golden Gate.

events.title: San Jose Veterans Day Parade (108th, largest in Northern California)
events.why: Held since 1918, this is the largest Veterans Day parade in Northern California and falls on a school holiday.

events.title: Veterans Day aboard the USS Hornet
events.venue: USS Hornet Sea, Air and Space Museum, 707 W Hornet Ave
events.why: A ceremony with guest speakers on the deck of a real aircraft carrier, plus full access to the ship on a day off school.
